h: Truth in the Words of Jacob

p: "וַיַּכִּרָהּ וַיֹּאמֶר כְּתֹנֶת בְּנִי חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ טָרֹף טֹרַף יוֹסֵף" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, לג).
— “And he recognized it, and said: It is my son’s coat; an evil beast has devoured him; Joseph is without doubt torn in pieces” (Genesis 37:33).
לִכְאוֹרָה הוּא פֶּלֶא,
— Seemingly it is an astonishing wonder
שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ אֱמֶת
— that Jacob our father, peace be upon him, whose quintessential attribute is Truth,
יוּכַל לָצֵאת מִפִּיו דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת!
— could utter from his mouth a statement that is not true!
גַּם לָמָּה כָּתְבָה הַתּוֹרָה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת?
— Furthermore, why did the Torah record a statement that is not objectively true?
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדִּיקְדְּקוּ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת א):
— And as they meticulously noted (Midrash Tanchuma, beginning of Parashat Toldot 1):
שֶׁגָּדוֹל הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁדִּבְּרָה הַתּוֹרָה דִּבְרֵי בְּדַאי בִּשְׁבִיל הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— that great is peace, for the Torah spoke fabricated words for the sake of peace,
וְאֵיזֶה? "כֹּה תֹאמְרוּ לְיוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית נ, יז),
— and which is it? “So shall you say to Joseph, etc.,”
וְאֵין אָנוּ מוֹצְאִים שֶׁצִּיוָּה וְכוּלֵי.
— yet we do not find anywhere that Jacob commanded this, etc.
וְאַף שֶׁאֱמֶת שֶׁהֵם שָׁלְחוּ כַּדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה לְיוֹסֵף,
— And even though it was true that the brothers actually sent these words to Joseph,
רַק כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱמֶת,
— yet because the message itself was not true,
לֹא הָיְתָה הַתּוֹרָה כּוֹתֶבֶת דִּבְרֵי בְּדַאי שֶׁלָּהֶם אִלּוּ לֹא לְלַמְּדֵנוּ שֶׁגָּדוֹל הַשָּׁלוֹם.
— the Torah would not have recorded their fabricated words were it not to teach us the supreme value of peace.
וְכֵן כָּאן: לָמָּה כָּתְבָה הַתּוֹרָה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֱמֶת?
— And so here: why did the Torah write a statement that was not true?
וְאַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה,
— And although it is not identical,
דְּשָׁם תֵּיבוֹת "אָבִיךָ צִוָּה לִפְנֵי מוֹתוֹ לֵאמֹר" הוּא דִּבְרֵי בְּדַאי וָשֶׁקֶר,
— for there the words “your father commanded before his death saying” were an outright fabrication,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כָּאן שֶׁכָּל הַדָּבָר אֱמֶת שֶׁאָמַר כֵּן,
— unlike here where it is entirely true that Jacob actually uttered this,
וּכְפִי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה בְּדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁהוּא הָיָה סָבוּר כֵּן;
— and in accordance with his perception, he honestly believed so;
אַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ לְהָבִין:
— yet nevertheless it must still be understood:
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהָיָה הַדָּבָר בְּטָעוּת וְלֹא הָיָה הָאֱמֶת כֵּן,
— since the matter was in error and the objective truth was not so,
לֹא הָיָה נִכְתָּב בַּתּוֹרָה דְּבַר טָעוּת!
— an erroneous claim would not have been inscribed in the eternal Torah!
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה אָמְרוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פד, יט):
— And for this reason they stated in Bereishit Rabbah (84:19):
נִצְנְצָה בּוֹ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ:
— the Holy Spirit sparkled within him:
"חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ" – זוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל פּוֹטִיפַר.
— “an evil beast has devoured him”—this refers to Potiphar's wife.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 2:1: “Accordingly one may explain what Judah said here, ‘and his brother is dead,’ which Rashi explains as a falsehood he uttered out of fear. Besides what we asked, it is difficult how Scripture could record false words that he spoke. Even if he said it out of fear, the Torah would not record a fabrication, as it says (Midrash Tanchuma, beginning of Toldos): ‘Great is peace, for the Torah spoke fabricated words for the sake of peace. Which? “So shall you say to Joseph…,” and we do not find that he commanded this.’ What is its difficulty? The event was true: the tribes did speak this way to Joseph. But since the matter itself was not true, even though they said it for some reason, the Torah would not have recorded their words, since they were fabrications. Perforce it comes to teach us that they acted properly in saying so for the sake of peace. If so, here, if Judah said something false out of fear, how would it be written in the Torah, when we learn nothing new from it? … And from this very fact, that ‘and his brother is dead’ is written in the Torah, and the Torah surely does not record fabrications, the holy Zohar and the Midrash Rabbah proved that Joseph was filled with wrath against Judah.”

There the truth is a momentary loss of the Holy Spirit in Joseph’s anger; here it is Joseph’s still unrepaired sin of evil speech.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 84:19: “‘Reuben returned to the pit, and behold, Joseph was not in the pit, and he rent his garments’ (Genesis 37:29). ‘Reuben returned to the pit’ – where had he been? Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua: Rabbi Eliezer said: In his sackcloth and his fasting. When he was free, he went and peered into that pit. That is what is written: ‘Reuben returned to the pit.’ The Holy One blessed be He said to him: ‘A person has never sinned before Me and repented, and you are the first to initiate repentance. As you live, your descendant will arise and be the first to initiate repentance.’ Who is that? It is Hosea, as it is stated: ‘Return, Israel, to the Lord your God’ (Hosea 14:2). ‘They took Joseph’s tunic, and slaughtered a goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood’ (Genesis 37:31). ‘They took Joseph’s tunic, and slaughtered a goat’ – why a goat? Because its blood is similar to that of man. ‘They sent the fine tunic, and they brought it to their father and said: We found this. Identify, please: Is it your son’s tunic or not’ (Genesis 37:32). ‘They sent the fine tunic…’ – Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The Holy One blessed be He said to Judah: ‘You said: ‘Identify, please’; as you live, Tamar will say to you: ‘Identify, please’’ (Genesis 38:25). ‘He identified it and said: My son’s tunic! A savage beast devoured him; Joseph has been mauled’ (Genesis 37:33). ‘He identified it and said: My son’s tunic’ – he said: I do not know what I am seeing. ‘My son’s tunic! A savage beast devoured him…’ – Rav Huna said: The Divine Spirit flashed in him: ‘A savage beast devoured him’ – this is Potifar’s wife.”

h: The Serpent and the Power of Slander

p: וְנִרְאֶה שֶׁבָּאוּ לְיַישֵׁב מַאֲמַר יַעֲקֹב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֱמֶת,
— And it appears the Sages sought to resolve Jacob’s statement so that it remains true,
אֲבָל עֲדַיִן קָשֶׁה:
— yet it remains difficult:
דְּהָא מַעֲשֵׂה אֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר לֹא הָיָה עוֹד,
— for the incident with Potiphar's wife had not yet occurred,
וְכָאן כְּתִיב "אֲכָלָתְהוּ" – לְשׁוֹן עָבָר!
— and here Scripture writes “has devoured him”—in the past tense!
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת, יוֹסֵף בִּירִידָתוֹ לְמִצְרַיִם הוּצְרַךְ לְתַקֵּן עֲוֹן לָשׁוֹן הָרָע שֶׁדִּבֵּר עַל אֶחָיו.
— However in truth, Joseph in his descent to Egypt was required to rectify the sin of evil speech he spoke against his brothers.
וְאִיתָא (עֲרָכִין טו:):
— And it is brought in Arachin (15b):
הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע מַגְדִּיל עֲווֹנוֹת כְּנֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת:
— one who slanders magnifies sins equivalent to three cardinal sins:
עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְגִילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים וְכוּלֵי.
— idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed, etc.
וּמִטַּעַם זֶה הָיָה כֹּחַ לְאֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר לְהִתְגָּרוֹת בּוֹ,
— And for this reason Potiphar's wife had the power to incite against him,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּיקֵּן עֲדַיִן פְּגַם דְּלָשׁוֹן הָרָע,
— because he had not yet rectified the blemish of evil speech,
שֶׁאָז הָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁכַּדִּין סִפֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם לְאָבִיו כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוֹכִיחֵם.
— since he still believed that he had rightly reported them to his father so that Jacob would reprove them.
וְאָז בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּיקֵּן קִלְקוּל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע,
— And at that exact hour, prior to rectifying the sin of evil speech,
אָמַר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ אֱמֶת: "חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ" – עַל הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁנִּקְרָא "חַיָּה רָעָה".
— Jacob our father spoke absolute truth: “an evil beast has devoured him”—referring to the serpent who is termed “the evil beast.”
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ: קִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד,
— And the root of the serpentine damage is envy, lust, and honor,
שֶׁמֵּהֶם מִסְתַּעֵף עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים,
— from which branch out idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed,
וְהַבַּעַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע מַגְדִּיל עֲווֹנוֹת כְּנֶגֶד שְׁלָשְׁתָּן.
— and the slanderer magnifies sins against all three.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "טָרֹף טֹרַף יוֹסֵף",
— And this is what he meant by: “Joseph is without doubt torn in pieces”:
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁיּוֹסֵף נִכְשַׁל בַּעֲוֹן לָשׁוֹן הָרָע בַּמֶּה שֶׁסִּפֵּר עַל אֶחָיו,
— namely that Joseph stumbled in the sin of slander in what he told against his brothers,
וְזֶה "טֹרַף יוֹסֵף".
— and this is the tearing of Joseph.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה, הָאַחִים שֶׁיָּדְעוּ שֶׁהֵם נְקִיִּים בָּזֶה,
— And through this, the brothers who knew they were clean of this,
חֲשָׁדוּהוּ לְיוֹסֵף לְפוֹסֵל בְּמוּמוֹ
— suspected Joseph of invalidating others with his own moral flaw,
וְסָבְרוּ שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי הוּא פָּגוּם,
— concluding that he was certainly blemished,
וּבִשְׁבִיל זֶה מְכָרוּהוּ לְעֶבֶד;
— and on account of this they sold him as a slave;
וַהֲרֵי גָּרַם גַּם לְאֶחָיו שֶׁיְּסַפְּרוּ עָלָיו לָשׁוֹן הָרָע,
— so he also caused his brothers to speak slander against him,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "טָרֹף טֹרַף יוֹסֵף"
— and this explains the double phrasing: “Joseph is surely torn.”
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה שֶׁנִּצְנְצָה בּוֹ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ "חַיָּה רָעָה" עַל אֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר,
— And this is also why Midrash Rabbah taught that the Holy Spirit shone within him identifying the “evil beast” with Potiphar's wife,
שֶׁזֶּה שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה יוֹסֵף תְּשׁוּבָה עַל עֲוֹן לָשׁוֹן הָרָע,
— for the fact that Joseph had not yet repented for the sin of slander,
שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמַר "חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ" כָּאָמוּר,
— concerning which Jacob said “an evil beast devoured him” as stated,
זֶה גָּרַם לְאֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהּ כֹּחַ לְהִתְגָּרוֹת בּוֹ,
— this gave Potiphar's wife the power to incite against him,
דִּבְרִית הַלָּשׁוֹן וּבְרִית הַמָּעוֹר מְכֻוָּונִים כַּיָּדוּעַ.
— for the covenant of the tongue and the covenant of circumcision correspond directly, as is known.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בַּנִּסָּיוֹן תִּיקֵּן הַכֹּל בְּמִצְרַיִם,
— And subsequently during the temptation in Egypt he rectified everything,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה הֵבִין שֶׁטָּעָה בַּמֶּה שֶׁסִּפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע עַל אֶחָיו
— for from this he realized that he had erred in speaking slander against his brothers,
וְתִיקֵּן פְּגַם לָשׁוֹן הָרָע,
— rectifying the blemish of the tongue,
וְנַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי הַנִּסָּיוֹן מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק.
— and through that trial he became the divine chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik.

h: Egypt as the Descent to Sheol

p: וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁאָמַר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם:
— And likewise what Jacob our father, peace be upon him, said:
"כִּי אֵרֵד אֶל בְּנִי אָבֵל שְׁאֹלָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, לה)
— “For I will go down to my son mourning into the grave/Sheol” (Genesis 37:35)
הוּא גַּם כֵּן דְּבַר אֱמֶת כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָא מִפִּיו.
— is also an absolute truth since it emanated from his holy mouth.
וְהוּא, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כֵּן יֻכְרַח לֵירֵד לְמִצְרַיִם,
— And that is, for through this he would be forced to descend into Egypt,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה נִתְיָירֵא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— over which Jacob our father, peace be upon him, had been terrified,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אַל תִּירָא מֵרְדָה מִצְרַיְמָה וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם מו, ג),
— and as it is stated: “Fear not to go down into Egypt, etc.” (ibid. 46:3),
וְאִיתָא (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עו, א) גַּבֵּי עוֹג:
— and it is stated in Bereishit Rabbah (76:1) regarding Og:
אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר "אַל תִּירָא אֹתוֹ" אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁנִּתְיָירֵא.
— Scripture says “Fear him not” only to one who was already experiencing fear.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "כִּי אֵרֵד אֶל בְּנִי אָבֵל",
— And this is what he meant by: “For I will go down to my son mourning”:
שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ אֲבֵלוּת שֶׁיִּסְבְּלוּ בָּנָיו בְּמִצְרַיִם זְמַן רַב,
— that he felt deep sorrow over the fact that his children would suffer in Egypt for a lengthy duration,
וְיִהְיוּ מְשׁוּקָּעִים בִּקְלִיפַּת מִצְרַיִם
— and would be submerged within the dark husk of Egypt,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "גּוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי" (דְּבָרִים ד, לד) – כְּעֻבָּר בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ.
— as it is stated: “a nation from the midst of another nation” (Deuteronomy 4:34)—like a fetus inside its mother’s womb.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "שְׁאֹלָה",
— And this explains his word: “into Sheol”:
שֶׁמִּצְרַיִם הוּא שְׁאוֹל – עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ.
— for Egypt is Sheol—the nakedness and licentiousness of the earth.
וְשָׁם הָיָה כָּל כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגָלוּת,
— And there the entirety of the Congregation of Israel was submerged in exile,
שֶׁעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז הֵ"א שְׁאוֹלָה (הֵ"א שְׁאוֹל),
— which is alluded to by the letter Hei of She'olah (the Hei of Sheol / Malchut),
וְיִצְטָרְכוּ לְהוֹצִיא מִשָּׁם הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כְּעֻבָּר בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ.
— and they would need to extract the Congregation of Israel from there where they lay like an embryo in its mother's womb.

p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיֵּבְךְּ אֹתוֹ אָבִיו" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, לה),
— And this is what Scripture states: “And his father wept for him” (Genesis 37:35),
וּלִפְשׁוּטוֹ קָאֵי עַל יַעֲקֹב,
— and according to its literal reading this refers to Jacob,
וְתֵיבַת "אָבִיו" מְיוּתֶּרֶת,
— yet the word “his father” appears superfluous,
דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר: "וַיֵּבְךְּ אֹתוֹ", וּבְיַעֲקֹב מִשְׁתָּעֵי!
— for it should simply have stated: “and he wept for him,” since it was speaking of Jacob!
אַךְ מְרַמֵּז: אָב יוֹ"ד וָא"ו:
— Rather, it mystically hints to: Av (אָב) plus the letters Yod (י) and Vav (ו):
דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ אוֹת וָא"ו, דְּאִיקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת,
— for Jacob our father corresponds to the letter Vav, which is called the letter of Truth (Tiferet),
וְיוֹסֵף – וָא"ו זְעֵירָא, וָא"ו הַמִּילּוּי,
— and Joseph corresponds to the smaller Vav, the Vav of the spelling fulfillment (Yesod),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קפב עַמּוּד ב),
— (as written in the holy Zohar Part I, 182b),
וְעַל יְדֵי יוֹסֵף הַהוֹפָעָה וְהַהֶאָרָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת,
— and through Joseph the supernal illumination flows down unto the attribute of Malchut,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קכג עַמּוּד ב): הֵ"א דָּלֶ"ת הֲוַת וְכוּלֵי.
— (as written in Zohar Part II, 123b: the letter Hei was originally Dalet, etc.).
וְיַעֲקֹב מוֹפִיעַ מִיּוֹ"ד עִילָּאָה עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת יוֹסֵף – יוֹ"ד זְעֵירָא מִשֵּׁם שַׁדַּי,
— And Jacob channels light from the supernal Yod through the attribute of Joseph—the small Yod of the divine Name Shaddai,
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁיּוֹסֵף נִפְרַד מֵעִמּוֹ,
— and as soon as he saw that Joseph was severed from him,
יֶחְסַר לוֹ הַהוֹפָעָה מִיּוֹ"ד עַל יְדֵי אוֹת וָא"ו,
— he realized he would lack the influx from Yod channeled through the letter Vav,
וְזֶהוּ: אָב – יוֹ"ד וָא"ו.
— and this is: Av (אָב) weeping for the flow of Yod and Vav.
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פד, כא) אִיתָא:
— And in Bereishit Rabbah (84:21) it is stated:
"וַיֵּבְךְּ אֹתוֹ אָבִיו" – זֶה יִצְחָק.
— “and his father wept for him”—this refers to Isaac.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לוֹמַר גַּם כֵּן
— And nevertheless it can likewise be explained
שֶׁזֶּה שֶׁהִשְׁמִיעָנוּ הַכָּתוּב בָּא לְרַמֵּז
— that what Scripture teaches us here comes to hint
שֶׁיִּצְחָק בָּכָה עַל בְּחִינַת יוֹ"ד וָא"ו
— that Isaac wept over the severance of the level of Yod-Vav,
שֶׁנִּסְתַּר יוֹסֵף וְיֶחְסַר הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לְמִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כָּאָמוּר,
— in that Joseph was hidden and the channeled influx unto the Congregation of Israel would be diminished as stated,
עַד שֶׁתִּיקֵּן שָׁם יוֹסֵף מַדְרֵגָתוֹ
— until Joseph rectified his spiritual rung there in Egypt
וְנַעֲשָׂה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— and became the divine chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik, Foundation of the World, as mentioned above.

paragraphs.text: Zohar Mishpatim 22:539: “We learned in our teaching: Hei was Dalet. When the male joined her, she conceived one son and is called Hei. Afterwards she gave birth and brought forth Vav, that son, who stands before her. Concerning this it is written, ‘A river goes forth from Eden’—it certainly issues from Him—‘to water the garden,’ to nourish it.” The surrounding discussion identifies Yud with Chokhmah and the first Hei with Binah. Rav Tzadok invokes the development of Dalet into Hei in explaining the illumination of Malchut.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 84:21: “‘All his sons and all his daughters arose to console him, but he refused to be consoled; he said: For I will descend mourning to the grave, to my son. His father wept for him’ (Genesis 37:35). ‘All his sons and all his daughters arose’ – how many daughters did he have? He had one, and if only he had buried her. It is, rather, that a person does not refrain from calling his son-in-law his son and his daughter-in-law his daughter. Rabbi Yehuda says: The tribes married their sisters. That is what is written: ‘All his sons and all his daughters arose to console him.’ ‘But he refused to be consoled’ – a certain noblewoman asked Rabbi Yosei, she said to him: It is written: ‘For Judah prevailed over his brothers’ (I Chronicles 5:2), and it is written: ‘Judah was consoled, and he went up to his sheepshearers’ (Genesis 38:12), and this one, the father of them all, ‘refused to be consoled’? He said to her: One is consoled for the dead, but one is not consoled for the living. ‘His father wept for him’ – this is Isaac. Rabbi Levi and Rabbi Simon said: When (Jacob) was with him he would weep, but when he would leave him, he would go, bathe, and anoint himself with oil. Why did he not reveal it to him? He said: The Holy One blessed be He did not reveal it to him and I will reveal it to him? Rabbi Simon said: This was based on: Anyone for whom one mourns, one mourns with him.”
